why: Tnfrsf4 is the mouse ortholog of human TNFRSF4 and encodes OX40 (CD134), a costimulatory TNF-receptor-superfamily member expressed mainly on activated T cells. Engagement of OX40 by OX40 ligand has been associated with enhanced T-cell proliferation, survival, and cytokine production.

OX40 is a target of agonist antibodies in cancer immunotherapy and of antagonist approaches in inflammatory diseases such as atopic dermatitis. Tnfrsf4-deficient mice are viable with altered T-cell responses in some models.
applications: Humanized TNFRSF4 (OX40) models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate OX40 agonists and antagonists in immunocompetent mice, sometimes combined with OX40L humanization.

why: Icos is the mouse ortholog of human ICOS and encodes the inducible T-cell costimulator (CD278), a CD28-family receptor expressed on activated T cells. ICOS binds ICOS ligand and has been associated with support of T-cell activation, follicular helper T-cell responses, and antibody production.

ICOS is under study as a target in cancer immunotherapy and in inflammatory and autoimmune disease. Icos-deficient mice are viable and show impaired germinal-center and T-cell-dependent antibody responses.
applications: Humanized ICOS models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate ICOS-directed agents in defined experimental settings, sometimes combined with ICOS-ligand humanization.

why: Ccr8 is the mouse ortholog of human CCR8 and encodes CC chemokine receptor 8, a class A G-protein-coupled receptor. CCR8 is expressed on certain regulatory T cells and other cells and has been associated with their migration and tissue localization.

CCR8 is expressed on tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells, and CCR8-directed agents are under study for selective depletion of these cells in cancer. Ccr8-deficient mice are viable with altered type 2 and regulatory T-cell responses in some models.
applications: Humanized CCR8 models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate CCR8-directed antibodies intended to target tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells in defined experimental settings.

why: LILRB4 (ILT3, CD85k) encodes an immunoglobulin-superfamily inhibitory receptor expressed on myeloid and other cells; the mouse genome contains related paralogs, including Lilrb4b. LILRB4 has been associated with inhibitory signaling and modulation of myeloid-cell and T-cell responses.

LILRB4 is expressed on monocytic acute myeloid leukemia and on myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and LILRB4-directed agents are under study in cancer. Mouse models have been used to study LILRB4-pathway biology.
applications: Humanized LILRB4 models, in which the human receptor is expressed in mice, have been used to evaluate LILRB4-directed antibodies and related agents in defined experimental settings.

Claudin-6 shows limited expression in most normal adult tissues and re-expression in several tumors, which has made it a target of CAR T-cell and antibody approaches under study. Mice with altered Cldn6 expression show epithelial barrier changes.

why: Muc1 is the mouse ortholog of human MUC1 and encodes mucin 1 (CD227), a transmembrane glycoprotein expressed on the apical surface of many epithelia. MUC1 has been associated with lubrication, barrier protection, and cell signaling.

MUC1 is overexpressed and aberrantly glycosylated on many carcinomas, and MUC1-directed antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates, vaccines, and cell therapies have been evaluated; clinical results have varied. Muc1-deficient mice are viable with increased susceptibility to certain infections.
applications: Humanized MUC1 models, which express human MUC1 (including tumor-associated forms), have been used to study MUC1 biology and to evaluate MUC1-directed therapeutics in defined experimental settings.

why: Il1b is the mouse ortholog of human IL1B and encodes interleukin-1 beta, an IL-1-family cytokine produced largely by myeloid cells. IL-1β is generated from a precursor by inflammasome-associated processing and has been associated with promotion of inflammation and fever.

IL-1β is implicated in a range of inflammatory and autoinflammatory conditions, and IL-1β-directed agents are in clinical use. Il1b-deficient mice are viable and show reduced inflammatory responses in several models.
applications: Humanized IL1B models, in which the human cytokine replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate IL-1β-directed agents in defined experimental settings.
Il1b knockout mice have been used to study inflammation.

why: Il18 is the mouse ortholog of human IL18 and encodes interleukin-18, an IL-1-family cytokine that, like IL-1β, is processed from a precursor. IL-18 is implicated in autoinflammatory and other immune-mediated conditions, and IL-18-pathway-directed approaches are under study; IL-18 binding protein regulates its activity. Il18-deficient mice are viable with altered interferon-gamma responses.

why: Ifnar1 is the mouse ortholog of human IFNAR1 and encodes a subunit of the type I interferon receptor, which together with IFNAR2 binds type I interferons. IFNAR1 signaling, through the JAK-STAT pathway, has been associated with antiviral and immunomodulatory responses.

Excess type I interferon signaling is implicated in systemic lupus erythematosus and related conditions, and an antibody blocking IFNAR1 is approved for lupus. Ifnar1-deficient mice are viable and show impaired antiviral responses.

why: Apoc3 is the mouse ortholog of human APOC3 and encodes apolipoprotein C-III, a small secreted apolipoprotein produced mainly by the liver. APOC3 has been associated with inhibition of lipoprotein lipase and with regulation of plasma triglycerides.

Loss-of-function APOC3 variants are associated with low triglycerides, and APOC3-directed agents are used or under study for severe hypertriglyceridemia. Apoc3-deficient mice show reduced plasma triglycerides, while transgenic overexpression raises them.
applications: Humanized APOC3 models, in which the human protein replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate APOC3-directed agents, including antisense and related approaches, in defined experimental settings.

fields.value: MHC class I-like Fc receptor (neonatal Fc receptor)

why: Fcgrt is the mouse ortholog of human FCGRT and encodes the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), an MHC class I-like receptor that binds IgG and albumin. FcRn has been associated with recycling and extended half-life of IgG and albumin and with transfer of IgG across cellular barriers.

FcRn blockade reduces circulating IgG and is used in antibody-mediated autoimmune diseases; FcRn also influences the pharmacokinetics of therapeutic antibodies. Fcgrt-deficient mice show reduced IgG and albumin half-life.
applications: Humanized FCGRT (FcRn) models, often combined with human albumin or IgG components, have been used to study antibody and albumin pharmacokinetics and to evaluate FcRn-directed agents in defined experimental settings.
